body:
## Problem and governing contract

Member fanout allocates a pending execution/lane wait for every undispatched roster member before admission. With a fixed window of8, increasing a prepublished roster from100 to1000 members grows outstanding lane-wait Promises **92→992**, while exactly8 admission callbacks are held and **zero member bodies have started**.

[DOM-3](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/c5802da/docs/spec/domain.md) states: **“Fanout memory is bounded by admitted work, not full corpus cardinality.”** This probe isolates concrete per-member queued execution state from roster storage/indexing and final report metadata. RUN-002's active window works in the measured cases, and ARC-005's abstract graph stays unchanged; those positive controls do not discharge the pre-admission state bound.

Severity: medium performance/scale. This is a concrete gap toward the specified scale behavior, not a post-run leak or a claim that a full per-member report can use constant space. Source publication finishes before instrumentation; this does not duplicate #160 array validation, #159 acceptance-history scans, or #172 context retention after completed work.

## Failing reproduction

Branch **`gap-hunt-dx@3a63e6c`**; production baseline `c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6`. [Probe, source analysis and complete controls](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/3a63e6c/scratch/gap-hunt/scale/FANOUT-ADMISSION.md).

From a clean checkout with Node24/npm and normal repository install prerequisites:

```sh
node scratch/gap-hunt/scale/repro-fanout-admission.mjs
```

The default command independently installs/builds generated packages, strictly compiles the generated-alpha fixture, runs type-aware lint, emits the six-row diagnostic and runs Jest. Expected baseline: **one control passes, one bounded-queue assertion fails** (additional pending waits900, allowance one active window8). Default clean replay was exercised; the supervisor independently repeated the six-row matrix and the same1pass/1fail Jest result against generated packages. No elapsed-time threshold is used.

| Population | Window | Held phase | Admission callbacks reached | Bodies started | Pending lane waits | Pending after hard stop |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|100|1|admission|1|0|99|0|
|1000|1|admission|1|0|999|0|
|100|8|admission|8|0|92|0|
|1000|8|admission|8|0|992|0|
|8|8|admission|8|0|0|0|
|100|8|body|8|8|92|0|

Each case reuses its prepublished roster (`sourceBodies=1`), reports the full population after cancellation, preserves topology and publishes no member result. An admission callback reached and held is not yet admitted work. The body-held control proves the active bound separately.

Node async_hooks counts the actual `new Promise` allocation in Supervision's permit-wait path and removes IDs on settlement; it retains only numeric IDs, never Promise resources. Positive path observation, population==window zero-wait control, held gates, and post-stop zero counts bound the interpretation. This is source-specific diagnostic instrumentation: moving/renaming the allocation site alone must not be reported as a repair.

Relevant source explains the result: Resolution eagerly uses `Promise.all(keys.map(... supervision.member(...)))`; each member awaits the lane pool; unavailable lanes retain a Promise plus grant/cancellation callbacks. Those are execution state, not roster indexing or final-report storage. The six relevant Resolution/Supervision implementation and contract files are byte-identical at merged `f43c587` (PR#171); this source comparison is recorded separately and is not claimed as a new merged-runtime execution.

## Numbered acceptance criteria

1. Bound outstanding per-member execution continuations/lane waits for undispatched members by the configured active window plus explicitly bounded dispatch slack, rather than creating one for each remaining corpus member. State the invariant and its owner in code comments/acceptance evidence; do not claim a bound on the necessary complete report or already-published roster.
2. Preserve the test-first failure at fixed window8 with populations100/1000. After repair, an outcome-equivalent instrumented diagnostic must discriminate the old linear queue from bounded scheduling state. If the implementation changes the counted allocation site, update and validate the instrumentation against a deliberate eager-enqueue negative control; never turn it green by ceasing to observe work.
3. Preserve useful parallel admission/execution up to the configured window: population>=window reaches the window under independent held work; population==window needs no extra queued member waits. Do not satisfy the memory criterion by serializing all independent work. No member body starts before its admission completes.
4. Preserve the declared/canonical start and report ordering, complete per-member status coverage, gate skips/refusals and the fixed abstract graph. Roster growth changes runtime members, not abstract operations. Members excluded or stopped before admission must not start bodies or publish results.
5. Hard stop releases queued dispatch and active lane waits and leaves no pending work/publication, including when admission is held and when bodies are held. Preserve soft-stop drain semantics, failure reporting, nested lane lending and priority reclaim; run the affected existing Supervision/facade tests as well as the new negative controls.
6. Keep Resolution's membership/current-evidence responsibilities and Supervision's admission/lifetime ownership intact. No new author batching, disposal or streaming obligation, public scheduling API, priority redesign, or weaker report contract is authorized. Escalate a concrete author-visible conflict if one is required.
7. Strict TypeScript, generated declarations and type-aware lint pass. Preserve real facade integration over a prepublished roster and synthetic held work. Record exact Node/OS/source and the diagnostic boundary; Linux and full150k/peak-heap qualification require actual evidence and are not established by these finite counts.

## Scope and dependencies

Pickup-ready internal bounded-dispatch work; no external API design choice is known to be required. Blocking dependencies: none. #155/PR#171 has merged and changes none of the relevant scheduling files. Coordinate shared source with other queue work, but #159/#160/#172 are separate mechanisms and do not block reproducing this issue.

Out of scope: total-corpus constant-space claims, source storage/key-index optimization, changing snapshot/report shapes, general streaming discovery, provider adapters, full150k capacity certification, paid calls, release automation and package publication. No fix PR is provided by the hunt.

## Attribution

Implementer: Codex gap-hunt worker (`gpt-6.1-sol`), operating for Mike North, wrote and ran the typed synthetic diagnostic and clean replay.
Agent assistance: Supervising Codex inspected the spec boundary, source/instrumentation and controls, checked live issues/PRs, and filed the implementation contract. No human implementation or review is claimed.
title: Member fanout queues corpus-sized execution state before admission
